newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks lower near close on record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks lower near close on record turnover.

text.p: Facing strong technical and pyschological pressure, Taiwan share prices turned sharply lower in the final minutes of trade on Tuesday on record turnover after blazing to an seven-year intraday high at the open.

With 10 mintues left or at 0350 GMT, the benchmark stock index had tumbled 120.8 points or 1.26 percent to 9,472.74, having seen an intraday high of 9,714.78 evaporate in heavy profit-taking and anxiety over central bank intervention.
Turnover shot to a record T$262 billion just moments before the close.
"The pressure was too strong. Also, the central bank's moves to mop up excess funds were obvious," Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang said.
Huange said electronics had risen strongly for some time and some investors were succumbing to a temptation to take profits.
Investors also were concerned about the central bank's moves to tighten banking-system liquidity to prevent excessive funds from flowing into the red-hot stock, she said.
The central bank has repeatedly issued negotiable certificates of desposit to tighten market liquidity.
On Tuesday, it issued T$8 billion worth of NCDs in what was widely seen as a move to temper the stock rally.
